nativeFacts.fact: Full-key strong SELECT on exact item sizes 1023/1024/1025/4095/4096/4097 bytes consumed 1/1/1/1/1/2. The 4097-byte item cost 2 when only pk was projected or a non-key predicate filtered it out; eventual read cost 1. Missing full-key reads cost strong 1 and eventual 0.5; missing partition SELECT cost strong 1.

Partition A's six items total 15360 bytes: strong partition SELECT cost 4, not the 7 obtained by summing individual point reads. Partition B's two 1500-byte items cost 1. Full/projection/filter-some/filter-none requests consumed identical capacity for each partition; eventual values were halved. IN across A/B partitions cost 5; IN across their sk=01 full keys cost 2.

A with Limit=2 returned three actual NextToken pages costing strong 1, 2, 3. Full items, projected keys and fully filtered empty results each had that same page cost sequence. These page-local costs total 6, versus 4 for the unpaged partition query.

The eight-item 18360-byte table scan cost strong 8, identically for full/projection/filter-some/filter-none, or eventual 4. Limit=2 filtered-empty scan pages cost 1,2,3,1,4; the terminal empty page cost 4. This differs from both simple whole-table byte rounding (5) and individual-item rounding (9). Physical-partition search/minimum overhead is not exposed; do not infer an exact general scan formula or partition count from this fixture.

The KEYS_ONLY GSI SELECT * and projected-key SELECT returned eight projected entries and cost 0.5 entirely on the GSI, with native Table.CapacityUnits=0. Requests for unprojected payload or filter attribute flag failed ValidationException without capacity. Limit=2 produced four two-item pages plus an empty terminal page, each costing GSI 0.5.

LSI SELECT * returned only projected pk/sk/l/flag and cost index 1, table 0, just like projected keys. Explicit payload projection fetched the six base items and cost table 7 plus LSI 1 (eventual table 3.5 plus LSI 0.5). A fully filtering projected flag predicate did not avoid the payload fetch: capacity remained 8. Keys-only filtered-none cost index 1, table 0. Classic Query payload-fetch control agreed. LSI Limit=2 keys-only pages each cost 1.

Batch projected full-key reads of 1023-byte, 4097-byte and missing items cost strong 4 and eventual 2. Transaction reads of those same keys cost 8 ReadCapacityUnits. All three operations returned one per-table ConsumedCapacity entry, not one entry per statement.

Initial INSERT VALUE ? with an M parameter was rejected because AWS requires struct syntax. Initial dependent write failures are preserved, not treated as successful capacity evidence. Calls beginning corrected- repeat the write matrix on a second uniquely owned base-only table using VALUE {'pk': ?, 'sk': ?, 'payload': ?}; both table lifecycles remain in the flat replayable calls array.

Corrected 1024-byte INSERT cost 1; grow-to-4097 UPDATE RETURNING ALL NEW cost 5; shrink-to-1023 UPDATE RETURNING ALL OLD also cost 5; DELETE RETURNING ALL OLD cost 1; deleting again cost 1. Successful RETURNING writes returned Items. Duplicate INSERT and failed conditional UPDATE omitted capacity; failed UPDATE returned the old item when requested. Omitted failure capacity is unknown, not zero.

Batch inserts of 1024/1025-byte items cost 3 and batch UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING cost 3. A mixed batch conditional failure plus successful 1025-byte insert returned aggregate CapacityUnits=3 but Table.CapacityUnits=2; preserve this native discrepancy rather than recomputing either field. Transaction inserts cost 6 WriteCapacityUnits and transaction update/delete cost 6. A conditional transaction cancellation returned reasons and the old failed item but no capacity; a subsequent strong read showed no canceled insert.
Both owned tables were deleted. DescribeTable returned ResourceNotFoundException for the indexed read table at call 102 and corrected-write table at call 127.

experiment.sizeRule: All seed attributes are ASCII strings. Size is sum of UTF-8 attribute-name and value bytes; storage/index overhead is not included.

limitations: Raw requests and modeled responses are CLI JSON, not HTTP bytes. Missing ConsumedCapacity is unknown, never zero.
No CloudWatch observations: failure-path capacity omitted by native responses cannot be inferred here.
A single tiny table does not establish physical-partition scan overhead for large or sparse tables.
Only recorded ASCII-string sizes, access paths and predicates were exercised; not arbitrary PartiQL semantic equivalence.
Limit pages are covered; no 1 MiB response/evaluated-data boundary is exercised.
GSI reads are eventually consistent; readiness observations and returned counts are recorded, not assumed.
